title: How to make a game with ai and that’s free
author: krazyalpaca
selftext:
Hi everyone,  
Just wanted to ask how to make a game for free with AI complete from start to end. I need to make this game as a project and I’ve written a story layout for it. Thanks

comments.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
comments.body: Just ask any AI chatbot this question and you’ll have your answer lol. Honestly though I think you need at least a basic subscription to get anything done. I’ve had good progress using Claude pro for $20 a month. I run out of credits / usage fairly quick though but end up with something playable

replies.author: krazyalpaca
replies.body: Ooh will definitely look into this. The main problem i feel is i may want it to end up on the app store/play store etc but i do have to use the right software for it right? Which gaming engine would you recomm3nd so my game could actually be played on the app store? Im so new to this if you cant tell lol

replies.author: Endlesscrysis
replies.body: Also ask this to a AI chatbot

replies.author: KillaNugs
replies.body: I think the game engine depends on what type of game you plan to design. There is unity, unreal engine, godot and some. Im pretty new to this as well. Im using Unity for my game. I like it and it's pretty easy to grasp.

replies.author: Neither_Berry_100
replies.body: You aren't spending 20 dollars on ai and getting a working game to sell lol.

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body: Not necessarily if you understand and use FOSS GAI tech. That is what I always advocate for. Its better than relying on corporate mainstream trash, let alone live-service scams.

replies.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
replies.body:
I have a bit of work to do on that front. I’ve been toying with ollama (just upgraded my PC so I was excited to test local AI (sad my 9070xt has some sort of driver issues unlike nvidia gpu’s)) and using models like qwen. I need to use them more because I felt like they were serious downgrades compared to opus.

Happy to take suggestions though. I need to improve my local set up.

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body:
I am still mastering that front myself. I already became accustomed to using Applio ever since I was disgusted at the anti-freedom EULA ElevenLabs tries to enforce against users of their service. Despite that they cannot truly enforce it against the law - transformative law prevents them from controlling copyright of any voices we clone from their software - since they are all GAI and thus far too transformative for anyone to copyright and control.

Same with Suno and Udio, so I am using music FOSS tools to workaround that.

I am still trying to do the same with art, but I had less reason since I already bought Retro Diffusion years ago for the pixel art. Now I just use FOSS GAI art tools for the more serious styles - realistic and stylized 2D and 3D graphics.

comments.author: Illustrious_Art_3774
comments.body: It will likely be good to start with a very simple idea. Since you have so many questions and do not even know where to start, make your idea as simple as possible. Strip it down to the bones. It doesn't much matter which engine you use, they all have their pros and cons, a chat bot can list the pros and cons of each, maybe watch a few basic videos on each and choose one (there are also lots of YouTube videos comparing the engines and asking that exact question: Which engine should you choose? Watch some of these videos if you want)

comments.author: That1guy4226
comments.body: Your best bet right now is to pick your preferred ai model. I recommend chatgpt or Claude for this, they both have options that can 100% HELP you make a game with limited dev knowledge. Start asking it how it can help you get started and what you'll need.

comments.author: Mustafag91
comments.body: Try Bezi if you're on Unity. Get at least the $20 sub and they have several models to choose from, if you write rules (use other AI for this) and write proper prompts, consistently switch threads to avoid cluttered context window, it can output good results and helps a lot in prototyping, building tools and systems. Give it a try, it easily integrates with Unity via plugin and has project context.

comments.author: h455566hh
comments.body: Like people sad use any AI, better payed 20$ version. Try some specialized dev AI's like bezi for unity or unreal engine specific ones.

comments.author: Robonotes1760
comments.body: If you have a Microsoft 365 subscription, you effectively get unmetered GPT 5.6 (probably Terra). It is not as easy as working with an MCP, but I have nearly completed quite a substantial game with it.

comments.author: Glittering-Pie6039
comments.body: "Hi can someone just make a game for me"

comments.author: Onye_Nacho
comments.body:
That is technically somewhat easy:

* Go download a FOSS engine, like [this one](https://www.redotengine.org/).
* Use the IAI (Informative AI) services - chatbots like Brave AI for guidance.
* Look into FOSS GAI options for art, code, audio, and voice acting. Most likely on Hugging Face.
* Spend as much time as necessary to make your wonderful game/work of art.

You'll make something decent and without spending a penny on corporate slop.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: Yeah - Claude is so good at this, share your story doc and as it the quickest way to get a basic game up and running. You can probably have something playable in about 15 minutes  if you have a focused initial interaction ok n mind.
